correctness.rationale: For every positive mode coupling s, integration of exact two-state population and coherence identities yields T(s)=2/gamma+(Delta^2+gamma^2/4)/(gamma*s^2); no approximations. Parseval and Tonelli extend it to every normalized finite-support upper-sublattice state and allow infinite mean. The only zero-coupling momentum at v=w has measure zero, so dominated convergence gives complete absorption. A polynomial has integrable critical quotient exactly when F(-1)=0; convolution factorization and a simple top singular value of the finite tridiagonal Gram matrix establish the unique sharp L-site bound. Poisson-kernel localization gives the nonzero F(-1) divergent prefactor; dominated convergence handles cancellation. Independent Lyapunov and Gram-matrix checker passes 231 comparisons. Numerical tests do not establish the all-L claim; the supplied analytic proof does.

value.rationale: The 2008 physically motivated walk is known to suffer critical slowing and divergent mean current dwell time from standard localized injection. Exact characterization of coherent preparations that avoid this divergence directly addresses the natural critical bottleneck without changing the Hamiltonian. The all-L optimal bound gives an operational state-preparation design, exact finite-size scaling and a unique sine envelope, not a renamed textbook algebra exercise; the Rayleigh result resolves a physically motivated nontrivial constrained optimization over infinitely evolving quantum dynamics. The proof also distinguishes complete eventual absorption from infinite mean lifetime, a significant boundary.
